items.prompt: Prove: A countable set has measure zero.
items.modelProof: Enumerate it as $x_{1},x_{2},…$ and cover $x_{n}$ by an interval of length $ε/2^{n}$. Total length $≤ε$.

$∫f_{n}$ increases to some $α≤∫f$. For the reverse, take simple $0≤s≤f$ and $0<c<1$, and let $E_{n}=\{f_{n}≥cs\}$. The $E_{n}$ increase to the whole space, so $∫f_{n}≥c∫_{E_{n}}s→c∫s$ (by 11.24 and 11.3). Let $c→1$ and take the sup over $s$.
Apply Fatou to $g+f_{n}≥0$ and to $g−f_{n}≥0$. The first gives $∫f≤\liminf∫f_{n}$, the second $\limsup∫f_{n}≤∫f$.

items.prompt: Let $f=1$ on $ℚ$ and $f(x)=x^{2}$ on irrationals, on $[0,1]$. Compute $∫f\,dm$. Is $f$ Riemann integrable?
items.modelProof: $∫f=∫x^{2}=1/3$. Not Riemann integrable: $f$ is discontinuous at every point of $(0,1]$, a set of positive measure.

There is no integrable $g$ dominating the sequence: $\sup_{n}n·1_{(0,1/n)}(x)≈1/x$, which isn't integrable. The integrals are all 1.

items.claim: Every set of measure zero is countable.
lines: A set of measure zero can be covered by intervals of total length $ε$ for every $ε$.
So it contains no interval of positive length.
A set containing no interval is countable.
items.explanation: “Contains no interval” does not imply countable. The Cantor set contains no interval and is uncountable.

items.details: Lebesgue integral 0 (equals 0 a.e.), not Riemann integrable.

items.name: $n·1_{(0,1/n)}$
items.details: Pointwise to 0 but every integral is 1. No integrable dominating function; Fatou is strict.

items.name: $1_{[n,n+1]}$ on $ℝ$
items.details: Pointwise to 0, integrals all 1. Bounded by 1, but 1 is not integrable on $ℝ$.
